limitations: One host, loopback; wrk and the origin run on the load CPU set, the daemon on its own set.
wrk is a closed-loop generator: its latency percentiles suffer coordinated omission under saturation. `bench latency` measures latency at equal offered load instead.
CPU time is user+system time of the daemon process from /proc/<pid>/stat (10 ms ticks), read before and after each run; the origin's CPU is not included.
Peak RSS is VmHWM after resetting it through /proc/<pid>/clear_refs before each run.
Hashcash at 8 bits with a session solved once per case; browser solve time is not measured.
No TLS, no WAN, no real browsers; a ranking on this host is not a ranking on yours.
Anubis runs with GOMAXPROCS equal to the Sibuna worker count, pinned to the same CPU set; its policy challenges every Mozilla User-Agent, with DNSBL and the honeypot disabled.
Hashcash work matched at 8 zero bits for Sibuna and 2 zero hex digits for Anubis. Anubis signs sessions with its default Ed25519 key, Sibuna with its keyed BLAKE3 MAC.
In forward-auth mode Anubis is asked at its check endpoint for the admitted and challenged workloads; the static and attack workloads reach its default answer, as in tools.py.
Anubis is the official release binary, outside this repository; its origin transport runs with Go's default idle-connection limits (no flags were changed).
Every run starts after fewer than 3,000 sockets remain in TIME_WAIT; a workload whose load generator could not connect is recorded as failed with the error text.
